column1: # The wajhs recitations actually name — الأوجه.
# `wajh` is the concept and has its dictionary entry: one of several manners of
# delivery, any of which may be taken within one riwayah or one tariq. The
# wajhs of the ten readings are far more than these, and that enumeration is
# not here. This registry is the narrower thing a recitation's label carries: a
# recording of Qalun is published «بقصر المنفصل مع صلة ميم الجمع» or «بقصر
# المنفصل مع سكون ميم الجمع», and a listener picks one by that label. Four
# wajhs and one more label cover what is named in practice.
# TWO PLACES WHERE THE RECITER CHOOSES
# The madd munfasil. Al-Nashr counts its lengths as ranks: the first is «قصر
# المنفصل» (1/321), where it reports a difference from Qalun, from Abu Amr and
# from others, and the third is «التوسط» (1/323).
# Mim al-jam before a vowelled letter. «واختلفوا في صلة ميم الجمع بواو
# وإسكانها», with both transmitted from Qalun (1/273); al-Nashr calls the two
# «وجهي الإسكان والصلة من ميم الجمع لقالون» (1/269).
# `excludes` names the other wajh of the same place: a recitation takes one of
# the two, never both. A wajh of one place is named together with a wajh of the
# other.
# The label says «سكون ميم الجمع» where al-Nashr says «إسكان». The row keeps
# the label's word, and `iskan_meem_al_jama` resolves through
# `alternative_spellings`.
# A WAJH CAN FOLLOW THE TARIQ
# For some riwayahs the choice is not open inside one tariq. Hafs reads the
# munfasil with tawassut by al-Shatibiyyah, and its qasr comes by other routes
# (al-Nashr 1/321: «وعن حفص من طريق عمرو بن الصباح»). The label is the same
# word either way, so the row is the same; the tariq is said by the
# recitation's tariq, not here.
# JAMA IS NOT A WAJH
# «الجمع» is the label of a recitation that does not choose: it recites the
# wajhs of a riwayah, or the riwayahs of a qiraah, together. Al-Nashr gives it a
# chapter of its own, «باب بيان إفراد القراءات وجمعها» (2/194). It is filed here
# because it stands in a label where a wajh would stand, and `kind` tells it
# apart: `wajh` for the four, `jama` for this one. A recitation labelled jama
# names no wajh beside it, so its `excludes` is empty.
# THE CODES ARE DERIVED
# Each name is derived from its vocalized Arabic by the standard's rules
# (rules 009 to 036), like every other term. `alternative_spellings` carries the
# forms in use. The short codes that file names use (`qsr`, `mdd`, `wmim`,
# `smim`, `jmea`) are in scripts/short-codes.json.
# `ref` cites al-Nashr, ed. al-Dabba, as volume/page.
